channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: A New Level of Threat and Fear Risks Pushing the U.S. and Iran Back to Full War
item.description: With new intelligence and the possibility of all sides seeking pretexts for action, the war in Iran is entering a dangerous phase ahead of elections in the United States and Israel.

item.title: NPR: The College of Magic turns ordinary kids into confident, top-hat wearing magicians
item.description: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

item.title: BBC News: Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection as service restored
item.description: The tech billionaire accuses Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using the network for military activity.

item.title: The Guardian: This comedian jokes about deportation from Ireland … but it is happening for real
item.description: Despite job offers, Jaishree Malik has had visa renewal and extension requests delayed and denied, and she is not alone Jaishree Malik bounds on to the Cheeky Monkey comedy club stage and brandishes an envelope – it is a…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi barrage near Mecca
item.description: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalate as fierce ground battles and a devastating siege strangle Yemen's Taiz.

item.title: Ars Technica: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
item.description: A new model suggests Mars may host ice-forming physics never directly observed before.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: She Was the DEA’s Premier Crypto Detective. The Clues Led Straight to Her Own Family
item.description: To escape the chaos of her Russian childhood, Lili Infante became an American law enforcement prodigy. She pioneered the DEA’s investigations of the dark web—never suspecting who she’d find hiding there.

item.title: WIRED Science: Scientists Trapped an Antimatter Particle for Months to Study Its Secrets
item.description: These elusive and reactive particles have been challenging to hold on to and even more challenging to study, but a new method paves the way for tests on the differences between matter and antimatter.

item.title: WIRED Business: What the US Movement Against Data Centers Can Learn From Abroad
item.description: Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale, has been tracking global data center development for years. The US has a lot to learn from what’s happened everywhere from Ireland to New Zealand.

item.title: The New Yorker: The State Officials Defending the Midterms from the President
item.description: Donald Trump has tried to purge voter rolls nationwide. Deidre Henderson, the Republican lieutenant governor of Utah, is among the chief election officers standing in his way.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Madame Clairevoyant: Horoscopes for the Week of October 25-31
item.description: For this week, and the remaining weeks of Venus retrograde, take time to reflect on where your relationships have felt unfair.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Everyone Knew About the A-Team
item.description: How did the Alexander brothers become real-estate elites while allegedly raping or assaulting more than a dozen women?

item.title: Mirror Indy: Help find the missing librarian at ‘Library of Legends’
item.description: Four artists created a live-action storybook adventure in Irvington for Halloween. The post Help find the missing librarian at ‘Library of Legends’ appeared first on Mirror Indy .
